simulation.statement: With a fixed seed and a fixed frame-counted control sequence, engine state is bit-identical to the pinned C++ oracle in every raw C4Fixed value, the Random/RandomCount/FRnd3 ledgers, landscape and material state, PXS execution, and C4Script VM semantics, except at the two accepted safety boundaries (sim-pxs-syncclearance, sim-s2-terminal-params). No intentional simulation divergence is retained by the profile, and every residual open gap blocks profile readiness until closed or proven unreachable.

evidence.note: The C++-golden primitive sections: fixed-point math, RNG ledgers, movement, PXS/mass-mover, material reactions, blast, script semantics (parity/README.md).
Rust self-consistency of the synthetic scenario snapshots.
A current-tree full-scenario C++ shadow diff is required. The historical Goldrush 15,000-frame report is scoped to its bundled Rust revision and does not satisfy this.
Historical continuous shadow differential; scoped evidence only, not a claim about the current tree.

control.statement: Control events reach the engine with C++ semantics: AutoStop key routing is exactly C4Game::LocalControlKeyUp, and in the profile the classic-set key-up release is suppressed exactly as in C++ (the normal-mode emission, ctrl-keyup-release, is profile-reverted). Host-side latency pacing (transport-presend-envelope) selects no different synchronized events.

evidence.note: Key-up delivery is synchronized and identical across control styles; classic movement stays latched.
The ACT rolling average and the 1..15 clamp stay bit-exact with C++; the divergent horizon sizing is pinned separately.
Real stock-C++/Rust host-client interoperation in both directions, including control delivery.

transport.statement: The port speaks the pinned C++ wire protocol: C4Network PID admission with the build check, ReliableUDP v2, and NetPuncher v1. The transport-quality divergences (repair interval, discovery intervals, announce repeats, PreSend sizing) are host-local or browser-local and change no synchronized data. Mixed C++/Rust connections are refused until real interoperation is proven.

evidence.value: crates/clonk-network (ReliableUDP, NetPuncher, and session protocol tests)
evidence.note: Wire-format conformance and version admission, including the C4Network2.cpp:1291-1299 build comparison.
Advertising and enforcing the profile during connection setup.
Real stock-C++/Rust interoperation, both directions.
What a released port build reads from this build's announcement and datagrams; landed for clonk-org/clonk-rs#471.

content.statement: Bundled content is exactly the pinned content commit, and the eight port-authored planet/System.c4g #appendto scripts are disabled, so definitions and scripts behave exactly as the shipped content specifies. Definition version gating prunes content newer than the engine exactly as C++ does.

evidence.note: Loads and applies every real scenario under content/ with real definitions and materials.
Fails closed when the content submodule pin drifts from this manifest, so a content bump must restate (and re-verify) the pin.
Content gating compares against the pinned engine compatibility version.

presentation.statement: Painter order, coordinates, sampling, blending, gamma placement, and resource state equal the oracle; GPU sampling is verified by readback against the software renderer with the documented one-byte cross-driver tolerance (docs/RENDERING_PARITY.md). Every opt-in presentation divergence is forced off and every first-run configuration default equals the C++ default.

evidence.note: Integer color formulas and resource state transitions tested exactly; GPU composition checked by readback against the software oracle.
Options, viewport, and GUI pixel parity against the C++ F9 captures.
C++/Rust presentation capture diffs for the profile.

save_replay.statement: Savegames carry the pinned C4XVer header and the C4GameSave component layout; recordings use the C4Record binary format (RCT_CTRL/RCT_CTRL_PKT/RCT_FRAME/RCT_END with 2-byte chunk heads). Interchange with a stock C++ build is claimed only as far as the stated differential evidence goes.

evidence.note: Chunk-head layout, 0xff filler framing, and the RCT_End truncation match C4Record.cpp:195-264.
Component order, player-info embedding, and group layout.
Differential check of save serialization and restore ordering.
Differential check of resync and post-mortem recovery.

divergences.summary: The default game tick is 26 ms (integer 1000/38) rather than the 28 ms application timer C4Game::OpenGame installs, so offline play and recordings advance about 7.7% faster in wall time; the state after a fixed frame/control sequence is unchanged.

PXS SyncClearance compaction: C++ copies a surviving chunk pointer downward without clearing the moved-from slot, aliasing one allocation into two slots (double processing, double delete); Rust transfers unique ownership and clears the tail. Rust's single-copy survivor order is authoritative at this undefined-behavior boundary.

S2 map-generator boundary inputs: C++ turns a negative Mandel alpha into a huge uint32 iteration budget, divides Gradient by a zero width, and takes a remainder by zero at alpha=-2. Rust bounds alpha to ten iterations, substitutes a denominator of one, and returns false from the raw algorithm. These inputs are excluded from the C++ differential runs.
Var(n)/Local(n) with a negative index: C++ clamps the index to slot 0 (C4ValueList::GetItem), the port's VM addresses a distinct __var_-1 key, so a negative-index read/writes differ.

A call into an object whose own script is already in flight starts from the pre-call local snapshot; C++ keeps named locals on the C4Object and the nested call would read them live. The overlay_foreign_cells pass replays earlier cross-object LocalN writes onto the snapshot and narrows, but does not close, the gap.
When a script callback errors mid-call, the port unwinds the call with its original argument values; C++ keeps the parameter mutations made before the error, so post-error parameter reads differ.

FindObject: the Layer condition is unmodeled on host objects (never matches) and shape tests use the vertices bounding box rather than the layered shape, so Layer-scoped or shape-precise queries can select a different object set.

ReloadParticle reports true when a reload passes all four C++ checks (network game, nil name, unknown name, missing Filename) and then fails on I/O; C++ reports false. The engine failure arm (clear every particle, remove the definition) runs identically on both sides.
A genuine containment cycle at scenario spawn time: C++'s two-phase denumeration keeps the mutual containment; the sequential spawn model breaks one edge and places that object uncontained.

After a definition-graphics reload, a live object that can neither re-resolve its graphic by name nor fall back to its own definition is left holding a dangling name; C++ AssignRemovals the object instead.

Network.ControlMode defaults to CNM_Async (2) instead of C++'s CNM_Decentral (0), which C4Config.cpp:540 calls the standard mode and C4GameOptions.cpp:93 labels async experimental. Only the default differs -- the mechanism is a faithful port -- but the value is synchronized, so it decides whether the host bounds its wait for a straggler and drops that client's input for the tick instead of pacing every participant on the slowest peer. The profile reverts it to the C++ default as a non-persistent overlay applied at session construction; the saved key is never rewritten.

Classic (non-AutoStop) control sets emit a synchronized Control*Released on key-up in both control styles; C4Game::LocalControlKeyUp routes a key-up only for AutoStop players, so C++ never delivers a release in classic style. The normal-mode emission lets scripts latch steering commands; the profile reverts it to C++.

Before a menu selection move, the port offers the horizontal COM_MenuLeft/Right pair to the object's script through OnMenuStep; in C++'s single-column menu the horizontal pair carries nothing the vertical pair does not. Inert for content that does not implement the callback and answer it true.

Network.MaxLoadFileSize defaults to 256 MiB in normal mode rather than C++'s 100 MiB so large classic definition families remain transferable; the LegacyClonk profile restores 100 MiB, and any explicitly configured host limit wins in either profile.

The host sizes the control PreSend horizon from a decaying delivery-time envelope instead of C++'s 1/150 EWMA of the mean control-send time, so a jittery link no longer stalls every participant on about half its ticks. Host-local: it changes which horizon the host picks, never which data is synchronized.
Reliable-UDP repair re-request damping is 250 ms instead of C++'s one-second iReCheckInterval; only a repair request that is itself lost is affected, and the synchronized repair stream is unchanged.

LAN game discovery probes on its own (shorter) interval instead of C++'s single 30-second countdown that refreshes the LAN list and the masterserver row together; the masterserver keeps the oracle interval.
A failed LAN reference query backs off for the error row's lifetime (C4NetErrorRefTimeout) instead of C++ re-probing a refusing host on every pass and stacking a duplicate row and connection attempt.

A host repeats its discovery announce on a burst interval after opening; C++ announces exactly once as the host opens and stays silent until probed, so one lost multicast datagram hides a C++ host until the browser's next probe.

Update and league HTTP runs on a configured reqwest client rather than a hand-written libcurl twin; the residual is that reqwest cannot emit an HTTP/1.0 request line, so a version-distinguishing server sees HTTP/1.1 with Connection: close.
planet/System.c4g/BirdFlight.c #appendto BIRD replaces the shipped four-coin-flip-per-tick bird steering with a continuous flight controller (separation plus weak alignment).

planet/System.c4g/EkeAirbikeSteering.c #appendto AB5B adds hold-to-steer airbike handling with a double-integrator float model; every test has an A/B twin pinning what LegacyClonk does with the append removed.
planet/System.c4g/EkeGpedRemoteControl.c #appendto SF5B keeps the pilot parked while the GPED steers an airbike, answering the stale Single-coms Jump'n'Run control would otherwise turn into movement.

planet/System.c4g/EkeGuidedMissile.c #appendto RL5B stops a guided rocket's turn when the steering key comes up; the shipped launcher latches the turn into the missile's command local until a straighten key clears it.
planet/System.c4g/EkeSftRelease.c #appendto SF5B completes the missing Control*Released pair for the Eke SFT's forwarded controls, so the airbike and the selected item learn a steering key came up.

planet/System.c4g/FoWReveal.c #appendto _FOW lifts Dragon Rock's map-authored shadow volume before a Clonk enters it; the shipped generator overrides the Clonk's own light and holds the interior objects inactive until it removes itself.

planet/System.c4g/MarsOrderCapsule.c #appendto BASE pays for a ClonkMars supply order atomically with an error report; the shipped commit spends one item at a time silently and abandons the rest when the first does not fit.

planet/System.c4g/GatherMenu.c #appendto CLNK adds a "Gather" context row to an owned crew member, offering one entry per loose item type the Clonk can both walk to and carry home, and queueing Get/Enter for each in one batch. LegacyClonk has no standing order of this shape, so a spare crew member is either driven by hand or left as a backup. The row issues ordinary player commands through the existing queue, exactly as if each had been given by hand, so every peer sees them through the normal control path; it is listed here rather than under port-only features because it does reach the control stream.
planet/System.c4g/MenuRangeRow.c #appendto MS4C collapses a ClonkMars range choice from three rows (value, Increase by 1, Decrease by 1) into one row with primary/secondary stepping.

Graphics.Remaster is the master switch for ten opt-in presentation divergences (HighDpiCursor, Mipmaps, SmoothLandscape, FineFogOfWar, HDExactBlits, ShaderLandscape, LoaderAspect, SnapTextToPixels, SkyDither, SmoothPresentation); each is off by default and the profile forces the whole family off.

Graphics.RenderInactive defaults to both bits (Fullscreen|Console) so an Alt-Tabbed game keeps drawing; C++ adapts Console alone. Only the default diverges: a written value is honoured verbatim and RenderInactive=2 restores C++ exactly.

The first-run application scale is seeded from the monitor's pixel density (rounded, integer); C++ starts every install at Scale=100, which on a 2x panel is an 800x600 device-pixel window with a 14px font.
The Options scale spinbox and slider cap at 400 instead of C++'s 300, so a 4x panel can express the classic 800x600 logical layout; the slider mapping and scale-test flow are unchanged.

Config.Graphics.Monitor selects the startup monitor; the oracle's SDL/GL build stores the row but never reads it back, so zero (the default) and every written value below it keep the pre-existing behaviour and only an explicit positive index diverges.

The startup main dialog draws the port's release version in C++'s exact placement, font, colour, and markup; C++ draws C4VERSION. Protocol identification and content gating still use the engine compatibility version.

The new-player dialog starts from the localized rank-0 name ("Novice" in English); C++ hardcodes the German "Neuling" and shows it to every language. The Player.txt omit-if-equal write default and the missing-Name= read fallback both stay "Neuling", so the file round-trips byte-identically with C++.

A presentation-detail governor drops fire-particle drawing and gamma steps automatically from measured cost; C++ exposes the same two steps (FireParticles, DisableGamma) only as static config. The governor skips the draw of a burning object's flames rather than stopping emission, so the engine's particle list is untouched and clients at different detail levels stay in lockstep.

One application pass may drain a clamped 250 ms simulation backlog but reserves a share of the pass for drawing; C++ runs at most one Game.Execute per pass and a machine slow enough to spend the whole pass in the simulation never repaints. Simulation state is unchanged by the split.
User-data directories are named "Clonk Rust" while the window caption stays "LegacyClonk"; a C++ install's user directory is not read or written by the port.

Config.General.MissionAccess is persisted as soon as the shared mission list the engine mutates differs from the file; C++ leaves the write to Config.Save() on a clean quit, so a round that ends any other way relocks a mission C++ would have kept.

port_only_features.summary: Proximity voice chat: microphone input, the push-to-talk rebind dialog, the port-only Voice.* config rows, and the "Audio" options-sheet group placed in the slack below C++'s own grid. No C++ counterpart; no game-control or lockstep effect.

The Graphics.ShowStats diagnostics overlay and its default-unbound StatsToggle key; C++ draws exactly one frame rate (game FPS) on the upper board and has no overlay. Presentation-only by construction.
The per-platform dock/taskbar icon; C4FullScreen has no reconciliation step to match.
F11 as a screenshot shortcut; C++ maps F11 as an ordinary physical key with no special role.

The in-app update flow: an incoming .c4u package is refused rather than applied (C++ extracts and executes its update program), an engine change gets its own message instead of reading as "no update", and the up-to-date case states the running version.

Windows icon slot 0 is the port's own mark generated from the logo; C++ puts lc.ico (LegacyClonk branding) there. The thirteen file-class icons are the engine's own, recovered from the pinned snapshot.

fail_closed.combination: A peer that does not advertise the profile, or advertises a profile version this build does not support.
fail_closed.behavior: Refuse the connection with the named reason; never fall back silently to the normal profile or to an unproven mixed session.

fail_closed.combination: A peer whose PID_Conn build number differs from the pinned build.
fail_closed.behavior: Refuse the connection; C++'s own admission rule compares only the build against C4XVERBUILD.

fail_closed.combination: The local content submodule pin or the in-repo planet tree differs from the manifest pins, or a scenario is loaded from any other content source.
fail_closed.behavior: Refuse to start in the profile; cargo xtask compat verify fails the gate on pin drift, so a content bump must restate and re-verify the contract in the same change.

fail_closed.combination: Any promise evidence is pending, or any divergence is open-gap/blocked, in the machine-readable manifest.
fail_closed.behavior: The profile may not be advertised as compatible (clonk-org/clonk-rs#498 completion rule); it is either not offered or offered as explicitly experimental, never as "legacy mode".

fail_closed.combination: A savegame, recording, or scenario whose C4XVer header or record type does not match the pinned engine version.
fail_closed.behavior: Refuse to load, exactly as C++ does; no attempt to repair or reinterpret foreign-version data.

fail_closed.combination: A saved configuration sets a profile-forced key (the Remaster family, RenderInactive, the scale cap, the first-run scale seed, or the game tick delay).
fail_closed.behavior: The profile value wins and shadows the saved value for the duration of the profile; the saved value is never merged in, and the normal profile is left untouched on exit.
